## Summary

I implemented the requirement that creating an owner identical to an existing one (same first name, last name, address, city, and telephone) is rejected with HTTP 409.

**Change — `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** (`src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):
- Before saving, `addOwner` now calls a new private `ownerAlreadyExists(owner)` helper. If an identical owner exists, it returns `ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT)` (409); otherwise creation proceeds as before.
- `ownerAlreadyExists` looks up owners by last name via the existing `clinicService.findOwnerByLastName(...)` and checks whether any match on all five fields. The check is scoped to the add path only, so `updateOwner` is unaffected.

**Tests** (`src/test/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`):
- Added `createOwnerDuplicateReturnsConflict`: posts an owner, then posts an identical one and asserts 409.
- Updated the pre-existing `createOwnerSuccess`: it previously posted "George Franklin, 110 W. Liberty St., Madison, 6085551023" — which is **seed data (owner id=1)**. Under the new spec that is a legitimate duplicate/409, so the test would have contradicted the requirement. I gave it distinct, non-duplicate data so it still verifies the 201-created path. (Its last name also had to remain letters-only to satisfy the existing name-pattern validation, which rejects the `nanoTime` suffix trick used by the direct-repository helper.)
